localScheduling.limitation: No retained local candidate array or per-action availability snapshot in run exports; candidate attributes alone are not dispatch authorization.

candidateCheckpointSummary.scope: Only checkpoints directly referenced by the selected unresolved item; this is not an exhaustive navigation-graph search.

findings.claim: The old USD generic scope has one match at source and none at current/Close-before/after. The generic USD candidate preserves URL, role, label, stableKey and targetBinding, while document-region label changes with document.title. The native USD button remains hidden and has a distinct role/region.

The browserSessionId and instanceScope differ from source. Same-instance continuity cannot suppress recovery; all 20 candidate checkpoints lack a current native history anchor and contain nonreplayable entry steps.

The actual classification projection exists on both sides with complete 58-node subtrees but both identityKey and conditionKey differ. No valid existing SDK classification correspondence was established. Current USD is outside the active modal; only after Close is it an active review target.

The selected strict checkpoint contains nonreplayable historical Return to observed page and Open Spot sub-menu. SDK performs one verified Close, then reports UNREACHABLE without claiming strict arrival or completing the USD item.

The persisted localSelections is 4, equal to the fairness limit. Current Close has supported native-button basis, resolved identity/target, visible/enabled true, replayable true and no recorded precondition blockers. It belongs to the active modal exit set.

Fairness can choose the stale remote review route over an otherwise ready local exit. The run does not retain the local candidate array or availability snapshot, so exact ready-local membership at selection time is not proven.
No omitted legal strict recovery route, safe classification reuse, replay authorization, or full recovery success is established by these reads.

recommendation.singleConclusion: Prioritize an already eligible and SDK-available exit from the active exclusive interaction boundary before remote recovery fairness, then reobserve and schedule again.
requiredGates: Use only current SDK availability plus the existing scope, uniqueness and local eligibility gates.
Require an exit belonging to the current exclusive boundary; do not infer from Close text.
Keep unknown-outcome, boundary-verification, retry and dispatch revalidation gates.
Do not change old USD review scope, mark it complete, transfer classification, reset remote debt or claim checkpoint arrival.
recommendation.notIncluded: Document-title-dependent review identity is a separate contract weakness. Existing identity/condition keys fail here; changing or ignoring region labels requires separately defined SDK evidence, not a scheduler shortcut.
suggestedSmallChecks: At localSelections=4, an eligible active-modal exit precedes a stale remote review route; post-exit scheduling rebuilds current facts.
An unavailable/ambiguous/stale exit or unknown outcome cannot gain priority or execution permission.
Absent an exclusive boundary, existing finite fairness remains unchanged.
A/B target changes and real context/region changes retain distinct unresolved work; no classification or coverage completion is granted.

limitations: No product code, browser, service, original task database, SDK host/batch, or test was run.
Only direct read-only SQLite handles with the existing entity decoder and pure classification/scope projections were used.
One classification helper launch failed import resolution before any database access; its correction is recorded.
No full observation, HTML, owner graph or task export was copied.
Current candidate attributes and later successful Close do not substitute for the missing selection-time availability/local-array evidence.
No timing or recovery-rate improvement is measured; the recorded recovery took approximately 23.9 seconds and still failed strict checkpoint arrival.
